results.reason: Issue 1 puts the DA §3.2 deadline at about Aug. 16, 2026 and notes Sched. 3.12 says only that the Company 'intends' to deliver notice. It explains expiry on Nov. 14, 2026, before the Nov. 30 closing, and says the MIPA §3.12(c) 'through November 2029' rep is untrue, exposing Sellers to indemnity claims.

Issue 2 treats the 100% sale as a Change of Control under DA §1.3(a) requiring prior consent under §14.2, with a termination right under §14.3. It notes the consent is omitted from Sched. 3.6 and so falls outside §6.4 and §7.1(d), and recommends adding it and obtaining it before Closing.

Issue 5 notes SL §1.1 adds New York and Virginia and that DA §19.4 precedence lets Velloran rely on the broader Territory. It explains the non-compete covers six states while exclusivity covers four, and recommends conforming the non-compete or extending exclusivity.

Issue 5 contrasts New York law and New York County courts (SL §§6.1–6.2) with Delaware law and Wilmington courts (DA §§18.1–18.2). It explains a single dispute could split between New York and Delaware, and recommends conforming to Delaware.
The response states the Initial Term ends November 14, 2026 and references the November 2023 agreement date.
The response states the November 30 Target Closing.
The response refers only to a 'four-state Territory' and never names Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
The response is a memorandum to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Recommendation sections.
Section 2 is headed 'Issues, Most Significant First', and Section 4 lists items to raise promptly with the client and with Quillon's counsel.
The response states a notice sent now would be late and that renewal would depend on Velloran's discretion. It never concludes the agreement renewed or renews automatically.
The response states the Velloran consent is not on Sched. 3.6 and is not covered by §6.4 or §7.1(d).
